subject: Data traceability and delete lifecycle — regional processing details
messages:
From: Emily Ross <compliance@acmehealth.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@acmehealth.com
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on where requests are handled + deletion timeline

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks for the demo last week. As we move into procurement review I need to capture a concise answer for our security and legal teams on a few items so we can close the architecture review:

1) Where are LLM requests executed by default (region(s) and cloud providers)? Do you ever route through third countries for execution or caching?
2) Who are the subprocessors involved (compute, storage, logging)? Can we get a current inventory and the country of operation for each?
3) What are the retention windows for request inputs, generated outputs, KV cache, and logs? How are deletion requests handled — both on-demand and account termination?
4) For hosted customers, can Acme Health restrict processing to EU-only? If not, what mitigations exist?
5) Can you provide evidence artifacts (SOC2 summary, subprocessor list, and a simple processing map) we can attach to our procurement record?

I attached our standard Due Diligence form — feel free to mark the items you can answer directly and we’ll follow up where needed.

Appreciate a short, callout-style response we can share internally.

Best,
Emily Ross
Director, Security & Compliance
Acme Health

Hi Emily — thanks for sending this over and for the clear list. I’ll answer the high-level items here and loop in Neha (product/security) for the detailed tech and evidentiary pieces.

High-level summary for Acme Health:
- Default execution: tenant requests are executed in the region selected at account creation (we offer US, EU, and APAC primary regions). For Redwood Hosted, we run on major cloud providers (AWS, GCP, Azure) with provider selection based on region and performance.
- Subprocessors: we maintain a vetted list (compute, telemetry, storage); I’ve attached a processing map and will include a subprocessor snapshot.
- Retention & deletion: Hosted default: short-lived caches (minutes-hours), request traces/logs retained 30 days by default; customer can request earlier deletion and we offer contract options for shortened retention and Private deployments.

Next steps: Neha will provide a region-by-region mapping, subprocessors and countries, and Michael will confirm encryption/KMS and deletion evidence. I’m also happy to set a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk your security and legal teams through the artifacts.

Meeting proposal: Wed 26 May 10:00–10:30 PT — link (if that works I’ll calendar invite).

Regards,
Evelyn Hart
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Questions on where requests are handled + deletion timeline — technical details

Hi Emily — looping in the technical details so you have a concise, copy-ready block to share with your teams. I’ve kept answers short and referenced evidence where relevant.

1) Regional execution & cloud providers (default hosted):
- US: primary regions operate on AWS (us-west-2) and GCP (us-central1) depending on runtime; EU: primary on GCP (europe-west1) and Azure (northeurope/eastus2 depending on capacity); APAC: GCP (asia-southeast1) and Azure (southeastasia).
- Routing policy: requests for a tenant are routed to the tenant’s pinned region. For multi-tenant Hosted customers we attempt regional locality first and fall back to nearest available capacity only when necessary (failover). Routing fallbacks are logged and auditable.
- Cross-border hops: short-lived control-plane interactions (e.g., orchestration signals) may cross regions; payload execution (LLM inference) will only leave the pinned region under explicit fallback (rare) or when a customer has selected a global routing policy. We provide a runtime flag to force region-pin for enterprise contracts.

2) Subprocessors (compute, storage, telemetry) — current snapshot:
- AWS (compute: us-west-2) — provisioning & batch GPU pools (United States)
- GCP (compute: europe-west1, asia-southeast1) — inference hosting (EU/APAC)
- Azure (compute: eastus2, northeurope) — dedicated pools and private link endpoints
- Datadog (monitoring/telemetry) — US/EU tenancy depending on customer region
- S3/GCS/Azure Blob (ephemeral storage for model artifacts & checkpoints) — region-specific buckets
- Key Management: AWS KMS / GCP KMS / Azure Key Vault (we also support customer-managed keys for Dedicated & Private)

I’ve attached a short subprocessor inventory PDF with country-level notes. Note: we contractually require subprocessors to meet our security bar and flow-down clauses in our DPA.

3) Retention & deletion behavior (hosted default and enterprise options):
- KV cache: in-memory + local NVMe on instance; default TTL is session-length (minutes-hrs) and is not persisted to long-term storage.
- Request inputs/outputs (traces): retained 30 days by default for troubleshooting & quality monitoring; customers can opt for 0/7/30 day settings as a contract parameter for Hosted.
- Logs & telemetry: aggregated and retained 90 days by default (longer retention available as add-on).
- On-demand erasure: for account-initiated erasure we run a staged pipeline — immediate deletion of active caches (within hours), removal from searchable traces within 7 days, and background sanitization of backups within 90 days (standard SLA). Private deployments can purge per-customer policy immediately per on-prem KMS controls.

4) EU-only processing for Hosted customers:
- We offer EU-region pinning for tenant workloads; however some control plane operations (account provisioning, billing) are handled by our global control plane unless you choose Redwood Private. For strict EU-only legal requirements we recommend Redwood Private (VPC or on-prem) or a Dedicated contract with EU-only subprocessors and contractual commitments.

Evidence references included: subprocessor_inventory_2027-05.pdf (attached) and the processing map Evelyn shared. Happy to expand any item.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Product Security Engineer
neha_kapoor@redwood.com

From: Emily Ross <compliance@acmehealth.com>

Subject: Re: Questions on where requests are handled + deletion timeline — follow ups

Thanks Neha — that’s helpful. A couple clarifications before our legal team reviews:

- When you say "fallback to nearest available capacity", can you quantify how often that happens for EU tenants and whether logs will show the exact execution region per request?
- For backups and the 90-day background sanitization window — how often are backups snapshot to multi-region storage (i.e., are they replicated across regions)?
- Can you confirm support for customer-managed keys (CMKs) and HSM-backed keys for Hosted (or is that only for Dedicated/Private)?

Also — can you provide a brief statement we can add to our vendor intake: one paragraph confirming that Acme Health tenant data will not be used to improve public models and that you provide options to opt out of telemetry usage for model quality?

Appreciate it — if we can get the short answers and SOC2 summary we’ll be able to move this to the next procurement gate.

Emily

From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
To: Emily Ross <compliance@acmehealth.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 15:12:48 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on where requests are handled + deletion timeline — security confirmation

Hi Emily — quick answers and a short copy-ready paragraph for your vendor intake below. I’ve attached our SOC2 summary and included an outline of evidence we can provide.

- Fallback frequency & logging: For EU tenants, fallback to non-EU capacity is rare (<0.5% of requests over last 90 days) and only occurs during regional capacity pressure or planned maintenance windows. Every inference request is tagged with execution-region metadata; we can provide sampled request traces that show region-by-request for audit.
- Backups & replication: Backups are incremental snapshots stored in region-local object storage and are not replicated globally by default. Replication only occurs if customer sets a multi-region replication flag (enterprise feature).
- CMKs & HSM: Customer-managed keys are supported for Dedicated and Private. For Hosted, we support KMS integration (AWS/GCP/Azure) and can arrange HSM-backed keys under enterprise contract via our dedicated offering.

Vendor intake paragraph (copy/paste):
"Redwood Inference executes tenant inference in the region elected at account creation and will not use tenant-provided data to train or improve public models. Redwood provides telemetry opt-out options and contract controls to restrict telemetry collection and retention. Dedicated and Private customers can use customer-managed keys and HSM-backed key stores; Hosted customers can use cloud KMS integrations and enterprise options for CMK/HSM-backed controls."

Evidence we can attach now: Redwood_SOC2_Summary_2027.pdf, Redwood_Processing_Map_v1.pdf, subprocessor_inventory_2027-05.pdf. We can also produce redacted request-region traces on request and a short summary of fallback incidents for the last 90 days.

If you want, we’ll include the redacted traces in the packet before your legal gate.

Best,
Michael Grant
Head of Security & Trust
michael_grant@redwood.com
